title: Liquidity Void Fill
summary: Marks wide, full-bodied displacement candles and signals when price later retraces into the void they left, at a chosen Fibonacci depth of the candle.
descriptionHtml:
A displacement candle is a bar that moves price a long way in one direction with little wick: the market traded through that range so quickly that few orders were filled inside it. That thin stretch is often called a liquidity void, and traders watch for price to come back into part of it. This study finds those candles and marks the bar on which price returns into them.

A candle qualifies when it passes every filter that is switched on. The ATR filter asks for a high to low range larger than the average true range times the multiplier. The body filter asks for the body to cover at least Body % Above of the range. The optional body size filter also asks for a range at least the multiplier times the previous bar's range. A qualifying bearish candle is recoloured light red and a bullish one light green.

From the newest qualifying candle of each side the study measures a level at Fib Value of its range: down from the high of a bearish candle, up from the low of a bullish one. A short signal fires when the high crosses up through the bearish level after a bearish candle has armed it, and a long signal fires when the low crosses down through the bullish level. Each signal draws a line at the level from the candle to the signal bar, and the optional time and date filters limit which bars may signal.
howToReadHtml:
A recoloured candle says a strong one-sided move has just happened and arms that side. A triangle above a bar is a short signal: price has rallied back into a bearish void, where sellers who drove the move may defend it. A triangle below a bar is a long signal: price has dipped back into a bullish void. The line shows the level that was reached and the candle it came from.

A signal only says price has returned to the level, not that it will turn there. Strong trends often run straight through a void, so traders usually look for a reaction at the level or combine it with structure before acting. A Fib Value nearer 0 puts the level nearer the start of the move, so price has to retrace further and signals come fewer and later; nearer 1 the level sits by the end of the move and is reached sooner.

settings.label: Long Signals
settings.html: Show the bullish side: the light green candles, the long triangles and their lines.

settings.label: Short Signals
settings.html: Show the bearish side: the light red candles, the short triangles and their lines.

settings.label: Fib Value
settings.html: How far into the candle the level sits, from 0 at the start of the move to 1 at its far end. 0.5 is the midpoint.

settings.label: Line Style
settings.html: Draw the fill lines solid, dashed or dotted.

settings.label: Apply ATR Filter
settings.html: Require a displacement candle's range to exceed the average true range times the multiplier.

settings.label: ATR Length
settings.html: Bars in the average true range used by the ATR filter. The filter blocks every candle until it has enough bars.

settings.label: ATR Multiplier
settings.html: How many average true ranges a candle must span. Higher values keep only larger candles.

settings.label: Apply Body % Filter
settings.html: Require a displacement candle's body to cover at least the set share of its range.

settings.label: Body % Above
settings.html: The smallest body as a percentage of the candle's range. At 80 the wicks together may be at most a fifth of it.

settings.label: Apply Body Size Filter
settings.html: Also require a full body and a range at least the multiplier times the previous candle's range.

settings.label: Body Size Multiplier (x)
settings.html: How many times the previous candle's range a displacement candle must reach when the body size filter is on.

settings.label: Apply Time Filter
settings.html: Allow signals only on bars that open inside the window below, read on the chart's clock.

settings.label: Time From (hour)
settings.html: The hour the signal window opens, on a 24 hour clock.

settings.label: Time From (minute)
settings.html: The minute the signal window opens.

settings.label: Time To (hour)
settings.html: The hour the signal window closes. A bar opening at the closing time is outside it.

settings.label: Time To (minute)
settings.html: The minute the signal window closes.

settings.label: Apply Date Filter
settings.html: Allow signals only on bars of the single date below, read on the chart's calendar.

settings.label: Day
settings.html: Day of the month for the date filter.

settings.label: Month
settings.html: Month, 1 to 12, for the date filter.

settings.label: Year
settings.html: Four digit year for the date filter.

faq.q: Why did a recoloured candle produce no signal?
faq.html: A side fires once per arming. After a signal the side waits for a new displacement candle, and a candle that arrives while a side is already armed only moves the level to the newer candle. If price never returns to the level, there is no signal.

faq.q: Do the time and date filters change which candles qualify?
faq.html: No. They apply only to the retracement bar that signals. Displacement candles are found and recoloured on every bar.

faq.q: Why are there no signals at the start of the chart?
faq.html: With the ATR filter on, no candle can qualify until the average true range has enough bars, so the first signals appear after that warmup.
